To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the massive increase in intracellular Ca2+ that occurs following the formation of C5b9 channels is responsible both for the rapid loss in mitochondrial membrane potential and for cell death.

the massive increase in ionized cytosol Ca2+ concentration, the dissipation of mitochondrial membrane potential and the cell death induced by lytic complement attack are all dependent on Ca2+ entry through lytic C 5b-9 pores.
C5b-91 induced cell death is associated with rapid and massive Ca2+ influx, mitochondrial depolarization and cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+ in the pathogenesis of the complement-mediated cell injury.
the role of Ca2+ influx and the resulting Ca2+ overload in the pathogenesis of the complement-mediated cell injury.
the mechanisms by which Ca2+ deregulates the mitochondrial membrane potential and causes acute cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ is the key factor in cell death, and that it is the [Ca2+]e, not [Ca2+]c, that is the critical factor.
C5b-91-induced cell death is the result of Ca2+ influx, which in turn is the result of a massive increase in [Na+]e.
the lytic C5-9 attack on nucleated cells results in a rapid and irreversible loss of cell viability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complement attack on nucleated cells results in rapid and massive Ca2+ influx, followed by cell death, which is mediated by Ca2+-induced mitochondrial permeability transition and cell necrosis.
the lytic C5-9 complex is a powerful ionophore for Ca2+.
the C5b-7 complex initiates the formation of a pore, the C9 polymerizes and forms a channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C5b-8 complex, which is the precursor of the C5b9 complex, is not cytotoxic.
the C5b-8 channel is the main mediator of Ca2+ influx and that the Ca2+ influx is the main cause of cell death in the C5b9 attack.
the complement system is a major effector of the immune system that is capable of killing cells in a very rapid fashion.
